title: Adaptive kernel launch strategy for attention ops (per-shape launch configs & safe fallback)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a runtime component that selects CUDA kernel launch configurations (grid/block sizes, dynamic shared memory reservation, and occupancy hints) for attention kernels on a per-request basis. The goal is to reduce p50/p95 latency variance across shapes and sequence lengths while avoiding regressions introduced by overly aggressive launch parameters. This work spans microbench harnesses, a small lightweight predictor for common shapes, telemetry-driven canary rollout, and explicit safe-fallback paths to baseline kernels.
tasks: Design: document safe parameter space for FA2/FA3 across common shapes (Confluence /docs/runtime/attn-launch-configs)
Microbench: add kernel-launch sweep harness to perf-runner for qkv shapes and head counts
Predictor: implement lightweight shape->launch-config mapping cache with LRU eviction
Telemetry: emit chosen-config + latency + mem-usage tags; add aggregation to console.metrics.attn_launch
Integration test: replicate synthetic long-context (8k) workload and verify fallback behavior under OOM
Canary rollout: staged rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback thresholds
Docs: update runtime tuning guide and add runbook for rollback and emergency disable flag
acceptance_criteria: Perf harness: end-to-end microbench shows non-regressive p95 for all tested shapes compared to baseline kernels
Safety: any OOM/rate of failed launches triggers immediate re-route to baseline kernel within 60s
Telemetry: per-config p50/p95 and error-rate dashboards populate within an hour of canary
Canary: automated rollback triggers when 95th percentile latency increases by >10% or error-rate rises >0.5% over window
Docs: runbook and tuning guide merged in docs repo
comments: 2026-01-12 — Rohit: Spike complete. Early experiments show a 3% p95 improvement on 8k sequences when using increased SM per-CTA for FA3 on A100. Observed occasional 1-2% regression on small batch sizes due to launch overhead; need heuristics to avoid change for tiny inputs.

2026-01-18 — Design review (Ava, Priya): Agreed to limit dynamic shared memory growth to +25% over baseline and to only enable advanced configs for batch_size >= 4 or seq_len >= 512. Added explicit ops that force fallback for auth-limited customers.

2026-01-22 — Rohit: Added microbench harness and pushed experimental results to https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1421 (WIP). Benchmarks available in CI artifacts: perf/eng/ENG-517202/*. We need a formalizer for the histogram merging logic used in telemetry.

2026-01-28 — Emily (SRE): Concern about memory fragmentation when reserving extra shared memory; we should add a GC-safe backoff and a flag to pin configs per-instance to avoid fragmentation churn. Also requested a canary that excludes Dedicated clusters until validated.
